name: dither-image

frames.best_why: Both photos are fully visible, showing the all-over dot screen and the mixed clean and dotted split.

tagline: Photos turned into coarse dot patterns, wiped clean by the pointer.
summary: A figure that renders an image as a black-and-white Bayer dither, plus a reveal variant where a clean copy is wiped across the dot pattern as the pointer moves.
appearance: Two square photos sit side by side on black. The left pug is fully rendered as a coarse black-and-white dot screen; the right mountain photo mixes clean colour with a dotted patch, split along a soft vertical edge. Tiny grey captions sit below.
behaviour: One photo stays fully dithered. Moving the pointer across the second wipes the boundary between the clean image and its dotted copy, and leaving resets it to the middle.
demo_content: A pug on a white wall and mountains above clouds, captioned Fully dithered, 16px Bayer cell and Partial reveal.
search_phrases: photo with retro dot pattern effect
halftone style picture for a website
cursor wipes photo to reveal colour
use_when: You want a printed, retro dot-screen look, or a playful wipe between colour and dithered versions.
avoid_when: The dither is grayscale and loses detail, so portraits and small frames turn muddy.
customise: src and alt fill each image; cell size, aspect, grayscale, contrast, brightness, blur, opacity, rounding and mask direction and range are props.
weight_why: Two images with CSS filters and one inline stylesheet; no script loop.

a11y.note: The partial reveal only responds to pointer movement, so keyboard users see just the default split.

issues: The reveal is pointer-only, so keyboard users cannot move the wipe.
The dithered layer drops all colour, so the effect suits textures better than detailed subjects.
polish_why: The dot screen is convincing and the wipe is playful; the pointer-only wipe is the one gap.
